sourcedFrom: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 (2024)
cleanIntro: The Hawkeye Alaskan is a hinged-FLOORPLATE, three-position-safety bolt rifle, and Ruger's Hawkeye book describes it by name in its General Information section: a medium-weight 20" barrel, a matte black weather-resistant finish and a Hogue OverMolded synthetic stock. ⛔ Routine cleaning needs only the bolt out and the floorplate open. The one part Ruger tells you never to take apart is the FIRING PIN ASSEMBLY — it is a permanent assembly under great spring pressure.

steps.title: Safety to LOAD-UNLOAD, then prove chamber AND magazine empty
steps.action: Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction and put the safety in the middle "Load-Unload" position — on full SAFE the bolt handle is locked down and cannot be raised. Then check, by eye, that the chamber AND the magazine are empty.
steps.prose: The middle position exists so the bolt can be worked without the rifle ever being on FIRE. Use it for unloading every time.
steps.aside: 2. CHECK TO BE CERTAIN THAT THE CHAMBER AND MAGAZINE ARE EMPTY.
steps.quote: 1. Keep the rifle pointed in a safe direction! Put the safety in the “Load-Unload” position.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly, step 1, p.20

steps.title: Bolt out — pull back and PIVOT THE BOLT STOP open together
steps.action: Open the bolt and draw it to the rear while at the same time swinging the bolt stop open. The stop is on the LEFT of the receiver on a right-handed rifle and on the right on a left-handed one. The bolt will not clear until the stop is out of its path.
steps.prose: Ruger says in the same step that this is as far as a routine cleaning needs to go, and that going further is rarely necessary.
steps.aside: This is as far as you need to dismantle the rifle for a routine cleaning. It is rarely necessary to proceed further.
steps.quote: To remove the bolt: Open bolt and pull to the rear while at the same time pivoting open the bolt stop which is located on the left side of the receiver on the right-handed version and the right side of the receiver on the left-handed version.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly, step 3, p.20

steps.title: ⛔ Firing pin assembly: out of the bolt is allowed, APART is not
steps.action: With the bolt out and the firing pin cocked, a pin or nail through the "disassembly hole" in the cocking piece holds the firing pin back so the assembly can be unscrewed from the bolt. Leave that restraining pin in until the assembly is back in the bolt. Never open the assembly itself.
steps.prose: Ruger gives three reasons in one caution: it is meant to be permanent, its parts are under great spring pressure, and special tools are needed to put it back together.
steps.quote: To remove firing pin assembly from bolt: With bolt out of the rifle and firing pin cocked, insert a pin or nail into the “disassembly hole” in the cocking piece.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly, step 4, p.21
steps.warn: CAUTION: The firing pin assembly is intended to be a permanent assembly and should not be disassembled. The parts are under great spring pressure and if disassembled could fly apart with sufficient force to cause serious injury.

steps.title: Stock off — open the FLOORPLATE first, then the front mounting screw
steps.action: Open the floorplate and hold it up out of the way, then loosen and remove the front mounting screw that holds the floorplate hinge assembly. Then take out the center and rear mounting screws from the trigger guard, remove the trigger guard and the magazine box, and lift the barrel and receiver out of the stock together, level.
steps.prose: If the magazine box sticks, Ruger says not to force it — it can come out with the barrel-receiver, carefully.
steps.aside: (If magazine box does not come out readily, do not force it.
steps.quote: To remove stock: Open floorplate and while holding it up out of the way, loosen and remove the front mounting screw
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly, step 5, p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Bolt out, and if you went further, the firing pin assembly out of the bolt (intact) and the barrel-receiver out of the stock. For routine cleaning Ruger asks only for the bolt out and the floorplate open. The trigger, sear and safety removal Ruger describes come under DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Ruger's own wording is that it is rarely necessary to go past the bolt.
steps.quote: 1. For routine cleaning it is necessary only to remove the bolt and open the floorplate.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Care and Cleaning, step 1, p.25

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Before going deeper: a lost spring or plunger is NOT substituted
deepSteps.action: The trigger, the bolt stop and the safety selector are all under spring tension. Work over a covered bench so a plunger that jumps is trapped, and if one is lost, replace it with the correct part. Never a substitute spring.
deepSteps.prose: Ruger suggests a shallow nap rug or an old coarse blanket on the bench, and a box for each part as it comes out.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: If a spring or plunger becomes lost do not use a substitute. Springs of correct tension are vital to the safe and reliable performance of firearms.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly — Warning, p.20

deepSteps.title: Trigger out — safety on FIRE, hold the trigger, press out the pivot pin
deepSteps.action: With the barrel-receiver out of the stock, put the safety selector on "Fire". Hold the trigger in place and press out the trigger pivot pin. The trigger is spring loaded, so keep your hold on it as the pin clears.
deepSteps.prose: The trigger/sear spring sits on a dimple in the trigger, which is where it has to go back.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the trigger: (Safety Selector should be in the “Fire” position.) While holding the trigger in place, press out the trigger pivot pin.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly, step 6, p.21

deepSteps.title: Sear out — pin out, receiver upside down, slide forward
deepSteps.action: Press out the sear pivot pin. Turn the receiver upside down and slide the sear forward. It drops out through the top slot in the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: It goes back in the same way: rear end (the end with the hole) into the slot from the top, then swung up and slid until the holes line up.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the sear: a. Press out the sear pivot pin. b. Turn receiver upside down and slide sear forward. Sear will drop out of the top slot in the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly, step 7, p.21

deepSteps.title: Safety assembly out — hold the selector, slide the retainer UP
deepSteps.action: Rotate the safety selector so its upper section sits fully over the center of the receiver tang. Hold it there with thumb and forefinger and slide the retainer up out of the receiver. Then lift out the selector, and take out the selector detent and its spring.
deepSteps.prose: The detent spring and plunger push against the bottom of the selector, so keep your fingers on it until the retainer is clear.
deepSteps.quote: a. Rotate the safety selector so that the upper section is positioned fully over the center of the receiver tang.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Disassembly, step 8, p.21
deepSteps.warn: Caution: Safety Selector is under spring tension from a spring and plunger acting against the lower section of the safety selector. The spring and plunger will jump out if not contained.

deepSteps.title: Long-term storage: strip it and keep the small parts in a tray
deepSteps.action: If the rifle will be stored for a long time, clean it thoroughly and take it apart only as far as the manual describes. Keep pins and other small parts that roll in a tray, re-wipe every surface with preservative oil, then reassemble.
deepSteps.prose: Ruger also says not to store the rifle in a leather case or scabbard. Leather attracts moisture.
deepSteps.quote: 6. If the rifle is to be stored for an extended period, clean the rifle thoroughly.
deepSteps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR RUGER® HAWKEYE® & GUIDE GUN BOLT-ACTION RIFLES (PM182) — PM182 / 11/2024 — Care and Cleaning, step 6, p.25

cleaning.name: ROUTINE — BOLT OUT, FLOORPLATE OPEN
tasks: Rifle and magazine confirmed unloaded first
Solvent-wetted patch push-pulled through the bore several times
Solvent-wetted bristle brush the FULL length of the bore, from the chamber end
Bore dried with clean patches and examined; brush again if still fouled
Clean solvent patch over every reachable surface in the receiver; toothbrush on caked dirt and the bolt

cleaning.name: OIL AND STOCK
tasks: VERY LIGHT coat of oil, inside and out — oil collects dirt
A drop of oil on the bolt parts, trigger pivots, safety, bolt stop and magazine latch
⛔ No acetone-bearing solvent near the stock finish
All solvent, lubricant and preservative wiped off the stock on reassembly
⛔ Bore clear of oil and grease before firing

cleaning.name: LEAVE ALONE
tasks: ⛔ The firing pin assembly is permanent — out of the bolt, never apart
⛔ A lost spring or plunger is replaced with the correct part, never a substitute

reassembly: Safety assembly, sear and trigger back in, if removed (detent and spring first, then the retainer slid down from the top).
Stock on: magazine box on the upside-down barrel-receiver, stock pushed forward to the receiver tang, trigger guard and floorplate assembly in, center and rear screws loose.
Barrel-receiver centered in the barrel channel, then the front mounting screw torqued to 90–95 in-lbs.
Center and rear mounting screws tightened alternately, a partial turn at a time, to 45–60 in-lbs.
Firing pin assembly screwed fully into the bolt until the bolt-sleeve flat lines up with the flat on the bolt handle; only then is the restraining pin pulled.
Bolt in: handle up, extractor lined up with the right-hand locking lug on a right-handed rifle, lugs into their channels, pushed fully forward.
fncheck: With no ammunition in the chamber or magazine and the rifle pointed safely: with the floorplate open, cycle the bolt a few times, close it, put the safety on FIRE and pull the trigger. Listen for the firing pin click, three times. On SAFE the trigger must not click and the bolt handle must not lift. On LOAD-UNLOAD the trigger must not click but the bolt must cycle. On FIRE it clicks and cycles. Push the follower up and close the floorplate. It must latch with a click. Press the follower down and confirm it moves freely. ⛔ Ruger warns that oil or grease even partly blocking the bore can damage the rifle and injure the shooter. Check the bore is clear before any live round.
